b.answer:
Worked example: Tolu locks Harvest Lane's front doors.

Connected apps removed (Google Account → Security → Your connections to third-party apps & services):

  • An old quiz app used once for a customer survey.
  • A free PDF converter that could see all Drive files.
  • A photo editor that could read and send email.

The Zapier connection was kept, because it's in use and listed in the access register.

2FA now on:

  • Business Gmail (ops@harvestlane), with an authenticator app. Backup codes are stored in the password manager.
  • Zapier account.

Sharing fixed: the Orders sheet was "Anyone with the link can edit". Now it's restricted to named people: Tolu (owner), the admin assistant (editor), riders (viewer). The former rider's address is no longer on the list.

Not included on purpose: no screenshots of keys, backup codes or 2FA QR codes.
mistakes: Removing an app connection that a live automation still uses, then wondering why it stopped.
Restricting link sharing but leaving former staff on the named list.
Posting a screenshot of the 2FA setup page, backup codes or a QR code as proof.
Only reviewing apps and not turning on 2FA, or turning it on for one account instead of two.
b.pass: A written list of at least three removed connected apps, two named accounts with 2FA on, and one sheet changed from link sharing to named people, with no keys or codes shown anywhere.
b.redo: Send it back if fewer than three apps were removed, only one account has 2FA, the sheet is still open to anyone with the link, or the evidence shows a code or key.

s.answer:
Worked example: Tolu's leak drill with an AI provider key.

Setup: Bitwarden (free plan) installed. New key named harvestlane-zapier-2026-10. Monthly spending cap $10, alert at $5. Stored in one Bitwarden entry with the key, created date and where it's used (Zapier connection from Track 1). It's not stored anywhere else.

Drill log (stopwatch running):

TimeAction
0:00Open the provider dashboard → API keys
0:40Revoke harvestlane-zapier-2026-10
1:30Create new key harvestlane-zapier-2026-10b; copy it once
2:30Replace the key in the Bitwarden entry; update the created date
3:10Confirm the old key shows as revoked in the dashboard
4:00Check the cap and alert still apply to the account
4:30Done

Result: 4 minutes 30 seconds. The old key no longer works (if you test it with a request, it returns 401). The new key lives in exactly one place. The clipboard was cleared afterwards.

One improvement: name keys by where they're used, so on a real leak you know at once which automation needs the new key. Once Track 1 starts, the key's working home is the Zapier connection, and the Bitwarden entry records where it lives rather than becoming a second copy in use.

Order matters: revoke first, then replace. A leaked key that is still live keeps costing money while you set up its replacement.

Evidence: the drill log, plus a dashboard screenshot with the key value hidden.
mistakes: Creating the new key before revoking the old one, which leaves the leaked key live for longer.
Keeping a copy of the key in a notes app or chat "just in case", so it has two homes.
Skipping the spending cap and alert because the provider hid the setting in billing.
Screenshots that show the key value as proof the drill was done.
s.pass: A password manager in use, a key with a spending cap and alert where offered, and a timed drill log showing revoke → create → update in one place in under 10 minutes, with proof the old key is revoked.
s.redo: Send it back if the drill took over 10 minutes or wasn't timed, the key lives in more than one place, the old key is still active, or any key is visible in the evidence.

Policy highlights (adapted):

  • We collect name, phone, appointment time and style notes. Birthdays only if the client chooses to share them for a birthday offer.
  • Booking data is used for appointments and reminders only. Promotions go only to clients who said yes.
  • Stylists see today's bookings; only Ifeoma and the receptionist can edit.
  • Keys live in the automation platform only. Build with test keys; only Ifeoma switches to live.
  • When staff leave, access is removed that day using the register.
  • Clients can ask to see or delete their data; Ifeoma replies within 7 days.

Incident card: first hour

  1. Revoke the exposed key or remove the person's access (Ifeoma).
  2. Create a new key and update it in its one credential (Ifeoma).
  3. Check usage, billing and the Paystack dashboard for unfamiliar activity (Ifeoma).
  4. Tell staff what happened and what not to use (receptionist).
  5. Fix the cause and update the register and policy (Ifeoma).

Submit: the register sheet, the one-page policy and the incident card.
mistakes: Leaving tools out of the register that hold customer data or money, such as WhatsApp Business or the payment provider.
Copying Harvest Lane's policy without listing what personal data this business collects and why.
An incident card with steps but no named person for each.
A policy that runs to several pages, so staff won't read it.
g.pass: An access register covering every tool that holds customer data or money, with access level and where each secret lives; a one-page policy that names the personal data collected and its purpose; and a five-step first-hour incident card with an owner for each step.
g.redo: Send it back if a money or customer-data tool is missing from the register, the policy is longer than a page or doesn't state what data is collected, or the incident card has no owners or doesn't start with revoking.
